parsed.title: Discussion on AI, Job Search, and Development Practices

topics.title: Automation of Job Search and Resume Generation

claims.text: P1 is preparing for a full‑time job search and is considering setting up cloud automation to generate PDF resumes tailored to specific vacancies.
P1 plans to configure OpenClaw to find vacancies, generate resumes, and write cover letters once the startup closes.
P1 states that in 2026 job seekers must add many AI‑related skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, embeddings, etc.) to avoid being filtered out by recruiters.
P1 notes that AI has become a market mainstream, and lacking AI knowledge makes job searching for JS/Python roles very difficult.

topics.title: AI Effects on Development Speed and Code Quality

claims.text: P2 claims AI accelerates development by having GPT write join queries and other code, reducing routine work.
P1 describes a case where AI‑generated raw SQL (450 lines) caused massive, inefficient queries and security issues, illustrating risks of over‑reliance on AI code generation.
P1 observes that cloud lowers the entry barrier to programming, leading to poorly optimized code being introduced into production.

topics.title: Speculation on the Future of Recruiters

claims.text: P1 expects the recruiting profession to become extinct, with HR functions reduced to internal personnel management.
P4 believes candidate search by keywords is even more detached from reality than before.

topics.title: Relation Between Question Quality and Answer Quality

claims.text: P4 notes that the quality of a system's answer is often proportional to the quality of the question and the amount of additional knowledge available.
